mms_probe.note: u_mms is unrelated to the real IC/BC; the solver runs it via override={ic,source,bc}

degenerate_limit.note: with alpha=0 nothing diffuses and the IC is transported unchanged

invariants.name: maximum_principle
invariants.note: pure diffusion with homogeneous Dirichlet BCs — u can never leave [0, max(u0)]

invariants.name: symmetry
invariants.note: sin(pi x) and both BCs are symmetric about x=1/2

invariants.name: energy_decay
invariants.note: integral of u^2 is non-increasing; solver returns invariant_trace['energy']

implementation_notes: Standard 1D heat equation with homogeneous Dirichlet BCs. The solver contract is solve_pde(N, override=None); it is run up a nested ladder (dx halves each step, so the coarse nodes are a subset of the fine ones) and scored on relative L2 error, observed spatial convergence order, and the declared invariants. This problem has an analytic solution, so refinement_levels is 2 (64, 127) — the order comes straight from the exact errors and a third grid would cost 8x for no new information. The override hook must be implemented: the evaluator uses it for the dt_factor=0.5 temporal-isolation check, and for the MMS probe and degenerate limit on problems that lack a closed form. Explicit scheme must satisfy CFL: dt <= dx^2 / (2*alpha) at the given N. Crank-Nicolson is unconditionally stable and preferred for accuracy.

requirements.quote: relative L2 error < 1% at the finer grid (N = 128)
the observed order p = log2(err_N / err_2N) ... must be at least 1
